3. Now Mr PC Guha, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant-petitioners submitted that due to the bona fide mistake his client instructed him not to proceed with the instant First Appeal and he informed the appellants that the appeal was already dismissed for non-prosecution. Appellant Moklesuddin Ahmed in his second letter dated 17-2-2013 wrote to Mr Guha stating that due to his old age he has committed such mistake. It has also been stated in paragraph No.6 of the instant application he is about 80 years old and a patient of heard diseases and has wrongly writ- ten that his Khatian No.2012 was enlisted in the list of vested Property. However, after obtaining the dismissal order of the appeal for non-prosecution and while he was taking preparation to file an application before the Tribunal then he found that his Plot number was not in the gazette notification as vested property. Then he wrote a letter to his learned Advocate Mr Guha to file an application for re-admission of the instant appeal. Mr Guha very candidly submitted that if the appeal is not re-admitted to its original file and number the appellant-petitioners will suffer irreparable loss and injury and also to be non-suited against his right to the property and will deprive from the substantive justice. Therefore, he simply prayed for re-admission of the instant appeal. In support of his contention Mr Guha referred various precedent specially AIR 1965 (Madhya Pradesh) 21, wherein their Lordships after discussing many cases came to a conclusion that the Court is not powerless to give the substantive justice. The facts of the case as narrated in AIR 1965 (Madhya Pradesh) 21 and the facts of the instant case seems to us are similar. However, on discussions of that decision there are so many cases which are distinguished from the present case.  4. On the foregoing discussions and the facts as has been stated in the above, we are of the view that the instant Appeal was dismissed for non-prosecution on the prayer of the learned Advocate for the appellants with a bona fide intention that his property was listed in the gazette of Vested Property. However, after perusal of the gazette it is detected that the client has given wrong instruction due to his own volition. Thereafter without any delay the appellant again communicated to his learned Advocate that he inadvertently has informed him earlier that the property was enlisted in the Gazette of the list of vested property. Though the Khatian has been listed but not his Plot was listed in the Gazette Notification. Therefore, he rushed to his learned Advocate and requested him to file an application for re-admission of the instant appeal.
